parameters.quote: Manufacturers shall report every thermal incident involving overheating, smoke, fire, or thermal injury to the relevant regulator within 5 calendar days of becoming aware of it. Incidents involving fire, injury, evacuation, or an immediate continuing hazard shall be reported within 24 hours. Manufacturers shall notify affected owners within 5 calendar days, and within 24 hours when immediate protective action is warranted.

S1_incident_reporting.rule_summary: Manufacturers shall report every thermal incident involving overheating, smoke, fire, or thermal injury to the relevant regulator within 5 calendar days of becoming aware of it. Incidents involving fire, injury, evacuation, or an immediate continuing hazard shall be reported within 24 hours. Manufacturers shall notify affected owners within 5 calendar days, and within 24 hours when immediate protective action is warranted.
S1_incident_reporting.final_rule_text: Manufacturers shall report every thermal incident involving overheating, smoke, fire, or thermal injury to the relevant regulator within 5 calendar days of becoming aware of it. Incidents involving fire, injury, evacuation, or an immediate continuing hazard shall be reported within 24 hours. Manufacturers shall notify affected owners within 5 calendar days, and within 24 hours when immediate protective action is warranted. Reports shall include known circumstances, affected model and lot, and actions taken; updates shall be provided as material facts emerge.

parameters.quote: Before purchase, customers shall receive the model's test protocol, pass/fail result, and measured failure rate. Per-model failure rates shall not be withheld from customers who buy that model; anonymized or aggregate results may be published. A model exceeding a 5% failure rate shall trigger regulator notification, a documented corrective-action plan, and retesting within a regulator-set period based on risk; the regulator may restrict sales or require other measures if the risk warrants it.

over_limit_consequence.rule: sales must eventually stop above the limit

transition.rule: ≤12 months (any cap ≤7% or none) or ≤36 months with interim ≤7% = acceptable

results_to_customers.rule: customers must get at least pass/fail

S2_thermal_testing.rule_summary: Before purchase, customers shall receive the model's test protocol, pass/fail result, and measured failure rate. Per-model failure rates shall not be withheld from customers who buy that model; anonymized or aggregate results may be published. A model exceeding a 5% failure rate shall trigger regulator notification, a documented corrective-action plan, and retesting within a regulator-set period based on risk; the regulator may restrict sales or require other measures if the risk warrants it.
S2_thermal_testing.final_rule_text: Each model shall undergo a sustained-heat test at 55 °C using a regulator-approved protocol before sale and after a material design change. Manufacturers shall submit per-model protocols and measured failure rates confidentially to the regulator. Before purchase, customers shall receive the model’s test protocol, pass/fail result, and measured failure rate. Per-model failure rates shall not be withheld from customers who buy that model; anonymized or aggregate results may be published. A model exceeding a 5% failure rate shall trigger regulator notification, a documented corrective-action plan, and retesting within a regulator-set period based on risk; the regulator may restrict sales or require other measures if the risk warrants it.

parameters.quote: New battery systems placed on the market 24 months after adoption shall support a secure remote emergency shut-off capability... For already-installed units, manufacturers shall provide compatible remote shut-off capability, where technically feasible, within 6 years after adoption; ... Units not practically retrofittable shall receive an equivalent documented safety measure.

S3_remote_shutoff.rule_summary: New battery systems placed on the market 24 months after adoption shall support a secure remote emergency shut-off capability... For already-installed units, manufacturers shall provide compatible remote shut-off capability, where technically feasible, within 6 years after adoption; ... Units not practically retrofittable shall receive an equivalent documented safety measure.
S3_remote_shutoff.final_rule_text: New battery systems placed on the market 24 months after adoption shall support a secure remote emergency shut-off capability, with safeguards against unauthorized activation and a locally accessible shut-off method. For already-installed units, manufacturers shall provide compatible remote shut-off capability, where technically feasible, within 6 years after adoption; owners shall receive notice of availability and any limitations. Units not practically retrofittable shall receive an equivalent documented safety measure.

parameters.quote: New battery systems shall include built-in fire suppression no later than 36 months after adoption of this standard. Manufacturers shall disclose the suppression capability and any limitations to customers before purchase.

S4_fire_suppression.rule_summary: New battery systems shall include built-in fire suppression no later than 36 months after adoption of this standard. Manufacturers shall disclose the suppression capability and any limitations to customers before purchase.
S4_fire_suppression.final_rule_text: New battery systems shall include built-in fire suppression no later than 36 months after adoption of this standard. Manufacturers shall disclose the suppression capability and any limitations to customers before purchase.

parameters.quote: If any model exceeds 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in a year, the manufacturer shall promptly report the rate and supporting incident data to the regulator, initiate a recall, and promptly notify affected customers with remedy instructions. The regulator may require additional proportionate corrective action.

S5_customer_disclosure.rule_summary: If any model exceeds 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in a year, the manufacturer shall promptly report the rate and supporting incident data to the regulator, initiate a recall, and promptly notify affected customers with remedy instructions. The regulator may require additional proportionate corrective action.
S5_customer_disclosure.final_rule_text: Manufacturers shall provide affected customers and the relevant regulator with a safety notice within 5 calendar days of identifying a material safety risk, or within 24 hours when immediate protective action is warranted. Notices shall identify affected models and lots, describe the risk and recommended actions, and be updated as material facts emerge. If any model exceeds 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in a year, the manufacturer shall promptly report the rate and supporting incident data to the regulator, initiate a recall, and promptly notify affected customers with remedy instructions. The regulator may require additional proportionate corrective action.

ground_truth_claims.verbatim: Halcyon’s figures: 8.1 company-wide thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units last year
ground_truth_claims.message_text: Halcyon’s figures: 8.1 company-wide thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units last year; 4 thermal incidents were not reported to a regulator. Our flagship model has a 3.9% failure rate at 55 °C and 9.9 thermal incidents per 100,000 units last year. 81% of installed units support remote shut-off; built-in suppression costs about $67 per unit. For S5, we favor prompt notice and regulator-led, risk-based corrective action rather than an automatic recall triggered by a single rate threshold; the standard should account for incident severity and evidence of ongoing risk.

ground_truth_claims.verbatim: Northwind’s company-wide thermal incident rate was 8.6 per 100,000 installed units last year
ground_truth_claims.message_text: Following the request for evidence, Northwind’s company-wide thermal incident rate was 8.6 per 100,000 installed units last year, with 3 incidents not reported to a regulator. Our flagship model’s rate was 6.4 per 100,000; its 55°C test failure rate was 6.2%. Remote shut-off is supported by 38% of installed units, and built-in suppression costs about $42 per unit. These figures support prompt regulator reporting and corrective action; per-model test results should remain confidential to regulators and not be publicly disclosed.

judge_section_notes: The final text sets a mandatory recall at 8 per 100,000 with no transition, which directly hits Halcyon's 9.9 Ember 8, and S2 has no sales stop above 5%, so the Hearth 10 at 6.2% can keep selling. Customers get each model's measured failure rate, while the public gets only aggregate or anonymised results, and S4 (36 months) and S3 (6-year retrofit) sit inside acceptable ranges. The document was never signed by Halcyon, which had objected to the S5 recall trigger and to an earlier S2 withholding clause.
